title: Louis Armstrong's range beyond the written limits
summary: Edison explains how Armstrong hit notes above what trumpet methods said was possible, leading into his Columbus visit.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: When Pops would come into town and he would be so sharp, you know. I remember before he -- you know, in his early days, you know the compass of a trumpet was from low C to a high C, and to play over this high C was absolutely impossible, like
Bach and Clark, they were writing, it's impossible to play over that. And here's a man that was hitting four or five tones over what they wrote that was impossible to do, he was doing the impossible.

So when he came to Columbus, Ohio the first time, my mother was a maid at the hotel downtown. And everybody loved her because she was diligent about her work and they all knew that she was working so hard to support me. So she asked the manager of the theater --
